title: Nitzavim: very nigh (Deuteronomy 30:11–14)
hook: the word is not in heaven or across the sea, "the word is very nigh unto thee"

segments.voice: Yesterday, shuv, the turning back. Your line was you can return. Today, how far away it really is.

Real wisdom must live on a mountaintop, or in a book you'll never finish, or with a teacher in another country. Real change must need a retreat, a new city, a fresh start in January. When something matters, it's tempting to put it far away. The distance protects you a little: if it's far, nobody can blame you for not reaching it. Moses takes that excuse apart in four verses.
screen: `ON A MOUNTAINTOP, IN ANOTHER COUNTRY.` → `A FRESH START IN JANUARY.` → `THE EXCUSE OF DISTANCE.`

segments.voice: "For this commandment which I command thee this day, it is not too hard for thee, neither is it far off. It is not in heaven." No one needs to climb up and fetch it. Nor, Moses goes on, is it beyond the sea, so that someone has to sail across and bring it back. "But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it." In thy mouth: you can say it. In thy heart: you can understand it. That thou mayest do it: you can live it. The Hebrew for near is karov. This verse has a second life in the Talmud. In Bava Metzia, the rabbis argue about whether a certain kind of oven can become ritually impure. Rabbi Eliezer is outvoted, and calls on miracles to prove he's right. A carob tree uproots itself. A stream flows backward. Finally a voice from heaven says the law is with Eliezer. Rabbi Joshua stands up and quotes our verse: it is not in heaven. The Torah has already been given; now it's decided here, by people, by the majority. The story ends with a report that God smiled and said, My children have defeated Me. Deuteronomy says: the Torah isn't out of reach. The Talmud adds: and once it's in your hands, it's yours to work out.
screen: `NOT IN HEAVEN.` · `NOT BEYOND THE SEA.` · `IN THY MOUTH, IN THY HEART.` · `RABBI JOSHUA AND THE OVEN.` · then, large: `VERY NEAR.`

segments.voice: Let your attention come in close: your breath, your hands, the room you're in. Then ask what good thing is within arm's reach today, not the big plan but the near one: a five-minute call, a kind word to someone in your house, an apology you already know the words to.
Nitzavim. Standing. And karov: near, very near, in your mouth and in your heart.
Your line: very near. In your mouth, and in your heart. That's day five hundred twenty.

howItsDone: 'It is not in heaven' (lo bashamayim hi) is taught as a principle of rabbinic law: questions of Jewish law are decided by sages through study and majority, as in the Talmud's story of the oven of Akhnai.

myth: the verse says the commandment is too hard for most people
'it is not too hard for thee, neither is it far off.'
in the Talmud, Rabbi Joshua answers a heavenly voice with this verse

fork.setup: a voice from heaven announces that Rabbi Eliezer is right, against the majority. you're Rabbi Joshua. what do you say?
fork.reveal: Joshua quotes Deuteronomy 30:12: the Torah has been given, and law is decided here by the majority. the story says God smiled.

original.note: Hebrew: near, close. 'the word is very nigh unto thee', Deuteronomy 30:14.

trapdoor: what you thought: a reassurance that the Torah is easy.
what it means: it isn't far away in heaven or overseas; it's in your mouth and heart, to do.
what a scholar hears: Bava Metzia 59b turns 'it is not in heaven' into a principle: law is decided by the human majority, not by heavenly voices.
recall: how good: opening the morning service
guess: standing, the whole people together before God
seated, the elders gathered at the gate
walking, the tribes on the road to the land

chat.says: Doesn't real spiritual wisdom take years of study somewhere far away?
options: Deuteronomy says it's not in heaven or over the sea, but in your mouth and heart.
Yes, the Torah says it waits on a mountaintop for the few who climb.
It says wisdom comes only through signs and miracles from heaven.
chat.meaning: Moses says the commandment isn't too hard or far off: the word is very near, in your mouth and in your heart.

Talmud.meaning: the rabbis' great collection of law and debate

Bava Metzia.meaning: a Talmud tractate; it tells the story of the oven

Eliezer.meaning: the rabbi outvoted even after his miracles

notes: Deuteronomy 30:11–12 and 30:14 quoted from JPS 1917 from memory; verify.

Bava Metzia 59b (oven of Akhnai): carob tree, stream, walls of the study house, heavenly voice; Rabbi Joshua cites 30:12; Elijah reports God 'smiled' (or laughed) and said 'My children have defeated Me'. Paraphrased; the walls are omitted for length.
karov glossed only as 'near'; the earlier 'same word for a close relative' line was cut as an unsourced word claim.
